title: Could Planet Labs Be the Next Palantir?
author: Parkev Tatevosian, Cfa
description: An analyst draws parallels between Planet Labs and Palantir, noting similarities in how both companies started with government contracts and expanded into enterprise solutions. Planet Labs stock has declined 67% from its high, while the article explores the company's growth trajectory powered by government contracts.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: The article presents an analytical comparison without strong bullish or bearish language. While it notes a 67% decline from highs, it frames this as a potential buying opportunity and draws positive parallels to Palantir's successful trajectory. The tone is exploratory rather than conclusive.

Used as a positive reference point for comparison, highlighting Palantir's successful transition from government contracts to enterprise solutions, implying this is a proven and successful business model that Planet Labs could replicate.

title: Got $5,000? 2 Growth Stocks Building the Software Backbone of the AI Revolution
author: Leo Sun
description: The article highlights Amazon and Palantir as two AI software companies positioned to benefit from the AI market's rapid expansion. Amazon's AWS provides cloud infrastructure and AI services like Bedrock and SageMaker, with additional upside from its Anthropic stake. Palantir offers data aggregation platforms (Gotham and Foundry) that enable AI application development. Both companies are expected to deliver strong revenue and earnings growth through 2028, though Palantir trades at a premium valuation.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: AWS is positioned as a linchpin of the AI market with strong growth prospects. The company benefits from Anthropic stake, expected 15% revenue CAGR and 24% EPS CAGR through 2028, and reasonable valuation at 25x forward earnings.

Palantir's data aggregation and AI integration capabilities position it as a key player in the AI revolution. Expected 58% revenue CAGR and 70% EPS CAGR through 2028 demonstrate strong growth, though premium valuation at 87x forward earnings is noted as a consideration.
Mentioned as a popular AI chipmaker focus, but the article positions software companies as underappreciated alternatives rather than endorsing or criticizing Nvidia.

title: CrowdStrike vs. Palantir Technologies: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
author: Pamela Kock
description: The article compares CrowdStrike and Palantir Technologies as investment options for 2026. CrowdStrike offers a leading cybersecurity platform with 22% revenue growth but remains unprofitable and faces reputational damage from a 2024 outage. Palantir demonstrates stronger financial performance with 56% revenue growth, profitability, and no debt, but carries higher valuation and customer concentration risks. The author recommends CrowdStrike for its better balance between growth and valuation, despite ongoing challenges.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong market position and resilient stock recovery post-outage, but offset by ongoing unprofitability (-3.4% net margin), reputational damage from July 2024 incident, and slower growth (21.7% YoY). Recommended by author as better value despite challenges.

Exceptional financial performance with 56.2% revenue growth, strong profitability (36.3% net margin), zero debt, high liquidity, and expanding commercial customer base. However, positive sentiment is tempered by high valuation multiples and customer concentration risk.
Mentioned as a third-party cloud infrastructure provider that CrowdStrike depends on, creating operational dependency risk. No direct investment recommendation provided.

title: Earnings Growth & Price Strength Make Palantir Technologies Inc. (PLTR) a Stock to Watch
author: Zacks.Com
description: Palantir Technologies (PLTR) has been added to the Zacks Focus List and is rated as a #2 (Buy) on the Zacks Rank.
